title: Rewrite track_dual_progress_reactivity_test.dart so it stops overriding the provider it claims to guard
why: Both tests replace trackDualProgressMetricsProvider's own body with a stub that independently calls ref.watch<int>(completionCommittedProvider) itself (lines 27, 69). A Riverpod .overrideWith fully replaces the provider's create function, so the real body in lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart:357 is never invoked by either test. Deleting that real ref.watch<int>(completionCommittedProvider) line today — silently breaking the dashboard/progress-hub's live refresh after a completion — would not fail either test in this file, despite the file's own docstring calling itself 'Regression test for Fix 3'. Contrast with the correctly-built sibling recent_activity_reactivity_test.dart, which drives the real production provider body over a real in-memory DB with no override of the provider under test.
recommendation: Rewrite using the recent_activity_reactivity_test.dart pattern: real in-memory DB, unmodified trackDualProgressMetricsProvider, seed a completion, tick completionCommittedProvider, assert the provider's actual output changes.
acceptance_criteria: Test constructs trackDualProgressMetricsProvider without overriding that same provider family
Test goes red when ref.watch<int>(completionCommittedProvider) is deleted from lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart:357
